response.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count FROM Orders o INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.date_order_placed >= '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND o.date_order_placed <= '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_order_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT gc.gender, gc.order_count, gc.order_count - ac.avg_order_count as above_average FROM gender_counts gc CROSS JOIN avg_count ac WHERE gc.order_count > ac.avg_order_count ORDER BY gc.gender

assumptions.assumption: Date range bounds are inclusive (>= and <=). The instruction 'compare as text' is treated as standard DATETIME comparison, since the provided ISO 8601 strings compare identically whether treated as text or datetime.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'compare as text' requires explicit text-based string comparison (rather than SQL's implicit datetime coercion), cast the datetime column to character.
